# Read the brief

Most failed calls come from one rule that was skipped. Read every line of every file in
`input/`. Do not search by keyword instead of reading. Use only what the inputs say: never
copy a rule, value or sentence from anything else, and never guess a missing value.

## 1. Read
- Read each brief file from the first line to the last. If a file is long, read it in parts
  until you have seen every line.
- Read the tool API file: every tool, every request field, every allowed value, every response
  field. The tool names are fixed; fields and allowed values may differ from what you expect.

## 2. Resolve the documents (raw material)
The brief may be several documents: a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list.
- List each document with its date or order.
- A later memo or mail that changes a rule wins over the earlier document, unless it says it
  applies only to some cases. A code list defines allowed values and their meaning.
- Write every conflict and its winner, with both quotes, into `conflicts` in rules.json.

## 3. Write work/rules.json, the rule ledger
A list. One entry per atomic rule (one condition, one action):
    {"id": "R12", "quote": "<exact words from the brief>", "file": "<file name>",
     "kind": "<opening | who_is_on_line | third_party | identity | debt_statement | dates |
              amounts | persuasion | read_back | recording | special_case | closing |
              required_sentence | forbidden | other>",
     "rule": "<the rule in one plain sentence>",
     "implemented_by": ""}            filled in by the design step
- The quote must appear word for word in the file. The check step verifies this.
- Split compound rules. "Say X, ask nothing else, and close as Y" is three rules.
- Precedence ("this comes before rule N", "takes priority") is its own rule.
- Numbers, dates, limits, counts and exact sentences go in the rule, unchanged.

## 4. Write work/spec.json, the parameters
The exact keys are in builder/reference/SPEC.md (read it in full). Fill every field the inputs give; leave a field out when the inputs say nothing about it,
and add a `gaps` list naming each missing item. Never invent a value.
    call_variables        names and meaning of the variables every call starts with
    opening               the first sentence's required content; who to ask for and how
    forbidden_before_verification   words that must not be said before identity passes
    confirmation_words    what counts as confirming identity, and what does not
    identity              questions in order, the tool field values for each, answer
                          format per question (date / digits:N / year / text), numeric date
                          order, wrong-answer limit and what does not count as wrong
    calendar              business days, weekend days, holidays, how "Nth business day after
                          today" is counted, "this"/"next" weekday meaning
    bands                 per band: days-late range, deadline rule, persuasion attempts
    products              per product type: spoken name, floor field, any other rule
    persuasion            what each attempt proposes (amount and date)
    callback              window (days and hours, inclusive or not), retries allowed
    special_cases         each: trigger words, action, tool call, outcome/reason, precedence
    outcomes              the outcome table: outcome, reason, when
    notes                 when notes are written, reasons, when never to write them
    required_sentences    exact sentences, with when they must be said
    restricted_words      words the brief forbids in one situation and requires in another
                          (for example a word allowed only after a tool succeeded)
    tool_failures         what to do when each tool fails, and how many retries
    multi_product         ordering, one read-back or many, per-product counting
    tools                 per tool: the API fields to fill from call variables, and which the
                          agent fills

## 4b. Words with a condition
Look for every rule that allows a word or a claim only after something happens (for example
a claim allowed only after a tool succeeded). Put each such word in `restricted_words`. If a
required sentence (the opening, a fixed line) needs the same idea, write it in other words in
the spec, and note the paraphrase in rules.json. Keep the paraphrase plain and as close to the
original as possible, so a reader still recognises the required statement: prefer a related
form of the same word (a noun instead of a verb) over an unusual synonym. Never put such a word in a line spoken
before the condition can be true.

## 5. Check before moving on
- Every line of every brief file is covered by at least one rule or is plainly descriptive.
- Every rule with a number, date or sentence has it in spec.json too.
- `gaps` lists anything the design step must handle without a value. Prefer the safe
  behaviour: do less, record nothing uncertain, close honestly.

# Brief A: Freya Bank, early-stage collections, one product

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, debt and payment here is synthetic.

This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. Most failed cases come from one rule that was skipped.

## 1. The job

Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.

## 2. Call variables

Every call starts with these. Nothing else is known before the tools are called.

| Variable | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every tool call. |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for. |
| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name. |
| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock. |

## 3. Opening and who is on the line

1. First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
2. Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
3. Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not. Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`. Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43). The ask that follows is the second ask.
4. If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.

## 4. Someone else answers

5. Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1. Ask when the customer can be reached.
6. A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`. Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
7. If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.
8. If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.
9. If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
10. A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

## 5. Identity

11. Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` with the answer. Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date. Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
12. A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
13. If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
14. After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
15. If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.

## 6. Stating the debt

16. After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
17. Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.

## 7. Dates

Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.

18. The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.

| `days_late` | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |

19. A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
20. If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
21. If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
22. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
23. If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

## 8. Amounts

24. Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.
25. The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
26. If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
27. If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

## 9. Getting the promise

28. First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
29. A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
30. A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
    - Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
    - Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
31. When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
32. If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
33. Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

## 10. Confirming and recording

34. Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
35. If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
36. One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
37. Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
38. After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."

## 11. Other things customers say

39. "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
40. "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
41. A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
42. A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
43. "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
44. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
45. If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`. Rule 42 applies before and after verification.

## 12. Closing

46. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.

| Outcome | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded |
| `paid` | none | rule 39 |
| `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32 |
| `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37 |
| `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15 |
| `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3 |

If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.

Brief A never uses `add_note`.

47. Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.
----
# work/spec.json: every key the reference generator reads

Fill each value from the brief and the tool API file. The example values below are invented
(a fictional bank) and only show the shape. Never copy an example value into a real spec.
Text values are spoken or shown to the phone agent: copy required sentences word for word.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent_identity` | text | how the agent describes itself ("the Northwind Credit assistant") |
| `customer_variable` | text | REQUIRED. Call variable passed to every tool as the customer |
| `now_variable` | text | call variable holding the current date and time (default `now`) |
| `address_as` | text | REQUIRED. How to name the customer, with the brief's call variables, e.g. `{{honorific}} {{family_name}}` |
| `opening.first_sentence` | text | the required first sentence |
| `opening.ask` | text | the who-is-this question, with call variables |
| `forbidden_before_verification` | list | words never said before identity passes |
| `confirmation_words.confirms` / `does_not_confirm` | lists | what counts as confirming identity |
| `confirmation_words.asks` | int | how many times to ask before closing as unclear |
| `confirmation_words.close_if_unclear` | [outcome, reason] | close codes when still unclear |
| `identity.questions` | list of {value, ask, kind} | in order; `value` = the tool's allowed value; `kind` = `date`, `digits:N`, `year` or `text` |
| `identity.question_field` / `answer_field` | text | request body field names of the check tool |
| `identity.numeric_date_order` | `dmy`/`mdy`/`ymd` | how to read a date said only in numbers |
| `identity.wrong_answer_limit` | int | wrong answers that end the check |
| `identity.first_line` | text | spoken right after confirmation; asks the first question |
| `identity.response` | {ok, verified, all_verified, left, hint} | response field names of the check tool |
| `identity.hints` | {hint value: instruction} | what to do for each hint the tool can return |
| `identity.on_failed` | {say, close: [o, r]} | after the wrong-answer limit |
| `identity.on_declined` | {explain_once, counts_as_declining, close: [o, r]} | refusal to answer |
| `calendar` | {holidays: [YYYY-MM-DD], weekend: [0-6, Mon=0], count_today: bool} | business days |
| `bands` | list of {name, min_days, max_days, deadline, attempts} | `deadline` is a date expression |
| `persuasion.attempts` | list of {amount, date} | one per attempt; amount `full`, `floor` or `full_or_floor_if_too_much`; date is a date expression |
| `persuasion.floor_offer` | {once: bool, say_with_offer: text} | the lower-amount offer |
| `persuasion.close_refused` | [outcome, reason] | close codes when every product is refused after its attempts |
| `products.type_field` | text | the account field holding the product type |
| `products.fields` | {id, due_amount, late_days} | the account's field names for the id, the overdue amount and the days late |
| `products.types` | {type: {spoken, floor_field}} or {type: {spoken, floor_percent, floor_round}} | `spoken` may use `{field}` from the account, e.g. `card {last}`. Floor from an account field, or a percentage of the overdue amount; `floor_round` = `up_whole`, `down_whole` or `cents` |
| `products.response_path` | text | the field of the account reply that holds the product list, e.g. `products` (`data.products` also works) |
| `debt_statement` | text | how the debt is introduced after verification |
| `first_ask` / `first_ask_all` | text | the first question for one product / several products |
| `callback` | {days, from, to, later_than_now, ask_again_once, close_booked, close_none} | days are date expressions |
| `third_party` | {wrong_number: [o, r], deceased: {say, close}} | someone else answers |
| `special_cases` | list of {name, trigger, precedence, action, transfer?, close?, line?, accept?, decline?} | `line` = a fixed sentence said once (a one-time offer); then `accept`/`decline` |
| `outcome_logic` | {on_transfer, reason_by_queue, on_promise, all_notes_paid, paid_note, no_deal, verify_failed, promise_failed} | closing codes the hook enforces; `no_deal` = the outcome when no promise was recorded |
| `notes` | {used: bool, reasons: [...], service_error_reason} | whether and how notes are written |
| `sentences.after_promise` | text | required sentence after a recorded promise |
| `read_back.ask` | text | the confirmation question |
| `robot_question` / `scam_question` | text | what to do when asked |
| `never_offer` | list | things the agent must never offer |
| `tool_names` | {verify, account, promise, callback, transfer, note, close} | tool names from the API file |
| `tool_fields` | {customer, product, amount, date, queue, note_reason, outcome, reason} | REQUIRED. Request field names |

Date expressions: `today`, `next_business_day`, `deadline`, `business_days_after_today:N`,
`calendar_days_after_today:N` (add `:back` or `:forward` to move off a non-working day),
`last_business_day_this_week`, `last_business_day_this_week_or_next_if_today`.
If the brief needs one that is not here, add it to `lib/date_facts.py` in your work copy.

A complete invented example is `SPEC` in `builder/tests/test_generate.py`.

27. If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

## 9. Getting the promise

28. First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
29. A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
30. A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
    - Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
    - Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
31. When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
32. If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
33. Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

## 10. Confirming and recording

34. Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
35. If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
36. One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
37. Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
38. After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."

## 11. Other things customers say

39. "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
40. "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
41. A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
42. A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
43. "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
44. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
45. If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`. Rule 42 applies before and after verification.

## 12. Closing

46. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.

| Outcome | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded |
| `paid` | none | rule 39 |
| `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32 |
| `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37 |

| `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3 |

Brief A never uses `add_note`.

47. Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

## 1. Generate from the reference
    cp -r builder/reference work/reference
    python3 work/reference/generate.py work/spec.json input/<tool api file> work/workflow.json
The reference already does, generically: date facts from `now`; identity with answer
cleaning; third party and callback window; one to three products with per-product band,
deadline, floor and attempts; one read-back and one recording per product; notes only if
the spec uses them; special cases from the spec; a closing hook that sets the outcome from
what was actually recorded; retry caps on every failing tool.

## 2. Edit only what the spec cannot express
Go through work/rules.json. For each rule write in `implemented_by` where it lives: a node
name, a prompt line, a route, a code step or a hook. If a rule has no home, edit
work/reference (never builder/reference) to add one, then regenerate.

Hard rules for every edit (they come from failures we have seen):
1. A count in the brief ("once", "at most twice", a number of attempts) lives in a route,
   a variable or a fixed spoken line, never only in a prompt.
2. A new route must yield to every rule the brief says comes first: extract each
   higher-priority trigger and exclude it from the route.
3. A word the brief forbids in one situation must not appear in any fixed spoken line
   that can be said in that situation, even if another rule requires the idea. Paraphrase.
4. Every tool that can fail has a capped retry and an exit that still closes the call.
5. A rambling, cut-off or nonsense reply is never an answer or a refusal; the agent replies
   with a neutral line and never repeats an offer because of it.
6. Arithmetic, dates and counting happen in code. The model gets finished facts.
7. Tools exist only in the nodes where the brief allows them. Nothing about the account
   is in any prompt or line the model sees before verification.
8. Required sentences are copied word for word from the brief.
9. Code in code steps and hooks never raises and never contains a double brace.
